correctness.rationale: Trace-class factorization gives tr(T_-T_+) as a nonnegative cross-domain sinc² integral; its time-domain form is a Fourier transform of a compactly supported triangular window. Uniform inverse-power expansion of the explicit frequency integral gives the exact inverse-square leading coefficient and cluster interval. Differentiation under its integral yields sign-resolved J' and J''; when LW is integer, the relevant triangular Fourier moment and its first derivative vanish, leaving a strict negative c^-3 term. For noninteger LW the first and second derivatives give unique alternating critical points at each sufficiently large phase half-period. Both exact integral formulas and derivative comparisons are corroborated by 117 standalone quadrature assertions; the analytical derivation is required for the quantified claims.

value.rationale: The quadratic spectral defect tr(T-T²) is a meaningful standard measure of departure from projection behavior and counts spectral leakage over all Slepian eigenvalues, not an artificial narrow statistic. For natural two-band geometry the result gives the sharp, dimensionful inverse-square interaction, complete subsequential coefficient interval, and a genuinely qualitative integer time-bandwidth boundary between eventual monotonicity and infinitely many local reversals. This phase distinction guides intuition for multiband spectral separation and is not implied by merely knowing that coupling vanishes as separation grows.
